concurrencyFinding.summary: G-120 (Overview lens) merged to main and deployed a few minutes into this build. It independently built the same 'filtered entry point tile' UI concept for Overview -- the exact thing CP1 flagged as 'shares the tile pattern' with this lane's attention row -- concurrently and without coordination.
concurrencyFinding.whatHappened: G-120's own first draft used a full-bleed overlay anchor over a plain .metric div and FAILED CI's real accessibility gate (color-contrast, reason 'bgOverlap': axe cannot resolve a background for text under a positioned box regardless of DOM order). Their fix made the tile itself the anchor: <a class="metric" href="..." data-filter="..." aria-label="...">. This lane's own attention row had independently built a different shape (a small <a class="go"> link line inside a plain .metric div) that, while not identical to G-120's failed draft, was a second implementation of the same tile-link concept.
concurrencyFinding.resolution: Rebased onto the post-G120 main and reworked this lane's attention row to G-120's established, CI-verified pattern instead of shipping a divergent second one. Also wired onto G-120's shared data-filter mechanism (resolveStaffLensQuery -> applyLens -> root[data-filter]) rather than building a separate URL-parsing path -- G-120's own close note named Development services as exactly the kind of 'destination lens' meant to consume it. Verified live both arms: a real matching status value pre-filters correctly; an unrecognised one (this lens's own WO overdue/due-today, which are computed non-status tiles) silently no-ops, matching the established discipline.
concurrencyFinding.corroboration: G-120's own 'Permits in flight' Overview tile links to /?lens=development-services&tab=pipeline&filter=active -- independent, concurrent evidence from a different lane that 'active' is expected to be a real Pipeline status value, strengthening (not proving) the open taxonomy finding below.
concurrencyFinding.lessonForThePlanner: Two lanes built the same UI pattern concurrently with no visibility into each other's work until a rebase forced the collision into view. A tile/entry-point pattern this broadly reusable ('fourteen of fifteen v2 destinations inherit it', per this lane's own dispatch) may be worth a shared-component note in the design system docs the moment a second lane needs it, rather than relying on each lane's dispatch to name the dependency and each lane to notice and reconcile at rebase time.

testResults.localSmoke: Started the server locally (PORT=8099) and drove it with a headless Chromium (playwright-core), not just unit tests. Verified: all 5 record tabs render on template-city AND on empty-city with no console/page errors; attention row tiles compute and navigate; tab-strip counts populate; the ONE table renders the approved column set per tab; the ONE load component renders Inspector/Manager/Officer load with real bar-chart cards; search + status + per-tab extra filters (type/manager/officer) actually narrow the table and update the result count; reset restores the full set; the Work orders List/Map/Performance segmented control actually switches views (Map shows the honest not-built state, Performance shows the SLA summary + daily queue); Plan review and Flood study render their honest not-built states with a basis.
bugsFoundAndFixedDuringSmoke: wireDsControls() was defined but never called at page init -- every filter/reset/pager control was inert (search, sort, manager/officer/type selects, view-mode buttons all silently did nothing; only the initial server-rendered table showed). Fixed by adding the call in the boot sequence.

dsRerender/dsLast were keyed by short names (wo/insp/ce/lic/pipeline) but wireDsFilterBar's control handlers looked them up by the FULL tab prefix (ds-wo/ds-insp/...); the mismatch silently no-op'd via optional chaining, so search/status filters and the pager APPEARED to load correctly (first render uses the correct key directly) but did nothing on user interaction. Fixed by keying both objects consistently on the full prefix.

A Next/Previous pager double-listener bug (page state incremented in a second listener that ran after the render already used the old page number, so Next required two clicks to visibly advance) -- caught in code review before the smoke pass, fixed by merging into one listener.

scopeDecisionsToReviewAtClose.decision: Attention row keeps the approved design's exact 6 tiles (WO active/overdue/due-today, Pipeline active/expiring, Plan review active) rather than substituting a different set, but 3 of the 6 (WO active, Pipeline active, Pipeline expiring) render 'Not read' because the underlying status vocabulary has no 'active'/'expiring' member -- see the taxonomy finding below. WO overdue/due-today ARE computed, off dueOffsetDays (a field that exists independent of the contested status vocabulary).
scopeDecisionsToReviewAtClose.confidence: deliberate, but the taxonomy gap underneath it is a real open question, not a resolved one

scopeDecisionsToReviewAtClose.decision: Filter bar simplified to ONE shared shape (search + status + reset) plus each tab's own extra selects named in its per-tab spec (Inspections: type, sort; Work orders: manager; Code enforcement: type, officer; Licences: type). Pipeline's 'All/Active/Requested/.../On hold' filter LIST and Work orders' 'Year'/'All departments' dropdowns from the approved mockup were not built -- simplified to the shared pattern given scope/time, stated here rather than silently dropped.

Pagination and filtering are client-side (fetch the full record set once via the existing /api/domains/:id route, slice in the browser) rather than a new server-side paged API. Correct for template-city's few dozen rows; for a real grant at Bastrop's real volumes (16,723 work orders, 12,683 pipeline cases) this means one large JSON response per tab load rather than a paged one. Not measured live against real data (G-122's incident makes live Bastrop reads unavailable to test against right now); flagged as a real scaling question for whoever owns this lens next, not fixed here.
scopeDecisionsToReviewAtClose.confidence: deliberate for this pass; a known limitation, not a defect introduced silently

openFindingForOperator.summary: The dispatch's per-tab metric-strip/filter category names for Pipeline ('active, requested, expired, expiring, pending docs, on hold') and Work orders ('active, requested, suspended, on hold, archived') do not match the already-shipped, tested status vocabulary in src/adapters.mjs (CASE_STATUS_VALUES: overdue/in-review/awaiting-applicant/ready-to-issue; WORK_ORDER_STATUS_VALUES: past-sla/at-risk/scheduled/closed).
openFindingForOperator.evidenceForWorkOrders: The approved design mockup's own Work orders table renders real status pills reading 'Active'/'Suspended'/'On hold', and src/mygov-live.mjs's mapRealWorkOrderRecord() already passes the live feed's raw row.status through UNMAPPED -- both point at 'active/requested/suspended/on-hold/archived' being the real MyGov vendor vocabulary, with the current fixture layer's past-sla/at-risk/scheduled/closed being an SLA-relative categorization a prior lane (G-91/G-92) built instead, under the same field name.
openFindingForOperator.evidenceForPipeline: Weaker -- only 'Active'(709) and 'Expiring'(18) are confirmed real category names via the attention-row mockup and the layout inventory doc's 'hero metrics' list; the full 7-item list could not be verified.
openFindingForOperator.whyNotFixedHere: Rewriting the core status enum is a breaking change to a widely-tested contract (dozens of assertions across src/domains-dev-services.test.mjs, src/domains.test.mjs, src/ds-render.test.mjs key off the current ids) and the source PDF this dispatch cites (SmartCity OS Screenshots (1).pdf, 18 pages) could not be rendered in this tool environment (pdftoppm/poppler-utils unavailable) to verify the true vendor vocabulary directly. Guessing a replacement would repeat the exact 'invented taxonomy' mistake this dispatch's own standing rule exists to catch, just with a different guess.
openFindingForOperator.recommendation: A lane with real image/PDF access (or the operator, who has presumably seen the real v1 screens) should confirm the true Work orders (and Pipeline) status vocabulary against the source capture before it is changed. If confirmed, work-orders.mjs/adapters.mjs need a genuine second field (the real vendor status, kept separate from the current SLA-relative categorization, which is real and worth keeping as its own dimension) rather than a wholesale replacement.
